children.name: Pontederia
children.description: Pontederia — a genus of liliopsidas.

children.name: Pontederia gigantea D.J.Sousa
children.description: The native range of this species is E. Brazil. It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Pontederia reflexa D.J.Sousa
children.description: The native range of this species is Bolivia to Brazil. It grows primarily in the seasonally dry tropical biome.

children.name: Pontederia crassipes
children.description: Pontederia crassipes (formerly Eichhornia crassipes), commonly known as common water hyacinth, is an aquatic plant native to South America, naturalized throughout the world, and often invasive outside its native range. It is the sole species of the subgenus Oshunae within the genus Pontederia.

children.name: Pontederia azurea
children.description: Pontederia azurea is a water hyacinth from the Americas, sometimes known as anchored water hyacinth. It is the type species of Pontederia subg.

children.name: Pontederia heterosperma
children.description: Distribution. Antilles (Cuba), Central America (Belize, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua and Panama) and South America (Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana and Suriname, Venezuela and Brazil - states of Acre, Amazonas, Amapa, Para, Rondonia, Tocantins, Alagoas, Bahia, Ceara, Maranhao, Paraiba, Pernambuco, Piaui, Rio Grande do Norte, Sergipe, Goias, Mato Grosso do Sul, Mato Grosso and Minas Gerais).

children.name: Pontederia paradoxa
children.description: The native range of this species is C. America, N. Venezuela, Brazil (Pará to Bahia). It is a hydroperennial and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Pontederia natans
children.description: Distribution. Angola, Benin, Botswana, Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Congo, Egypt, Ethiopia, Gabon, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Ivory Coast, Liberia, Madagascar, Mali, Mozambique, Niger, Nigeria, Rwanda, Senegal, Sierra Leone, South Sudan, Sudan, Tanzania, Togo, Uganda, Zaire, Zambia and Zimbabwe.

children.name: Pontederia diversifolia
children.description: Distribution. Antilles (Cuba, Dominican Republic, and Puerto Rico), Central America (Belize, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua and Panama) and South America (Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, Venezuela and Brazil - states of Acre, Amazonas, Amapa, Para, Rondonia, Roraima, Tocantins, Alagoas, Bahia, Ceara, Maranhao, Paraiba, Pernambuco, Piaui, Rio Grande do Norte, Sergipe, Goias, Mato Grosso do Sul, Mato Grosso, Minas Gerais and Rio de Janeiro).

children.name: Pontederia paniculata
children.description: Distribution. Pontederia paniculata possesses a peculiarly disjunctive distribution between North-eastern Brazil (states of Alagoas, Bahia, Ceara, Paraiba, Pernambuco, Rio Grande do Norte and Sergipe), north-western South America (Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana and Venezuela), Central America (Nicaragua), Antilles (Cuba and Jamaica) and North America (Mexico).

children.name: Pontederia cordata
children.description: Pontederia cordata, common name pickerelweed (USA) or pickerel weed (UK), is a monocotyledonous aquatic plant native to the Americas.

children.name: Pontederia parviflora
children.description: Distribution. Panama, Venezuela, Colombia and Brazil (states of Tocantins, Alagoas, Ceara, Maranhao, Paraiba, Pernambuco, Piaui, Distrito Federal, Goias, Mato Grosso do Sul, Mato Grosso, Minas Gerais and Sao Paulo).

children.name: Pontederia triflora
children.description: Distribution. Colombia, Venezuela, Guyana, Bolivia, Argentina and Brazil (states of Roraima, Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul and Minas Gerais).

children.name: Pontederia rotundifolia
children.description: Note: See discussion by Horn & Haynes (in Taxon 36: 623. 1987), who concur with Lowden's type choice.

children.name: Pontederia subovata
children.description: Distribution. Venezuela, Guyana, Bolivia, Argentina, Paraguay and Brazil (states of Acre, Amazonas, Amapa, Para, Tocantins, Bahia, Piaui, Goias, Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul, Minas Gerais, Sao Paulo, Parana, Rio Grande do Sul and Santa Catarina).

children.name: Pontederia vaginalis
children.description: Monochoria vaginalis is a species of flowering plant in the water hyacinth family known by several common names, including heartshape false pickerelweed and oval-leafed pondweed. It is native to much of Asia and across many of the Pacific Islands, and it is known in other areas as an introduced species.

children.name: Pontederia plantaginea
children.description: Distribution. Australia, Bangladesh, Cambodia, China, India, Indonesia, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Thailand and Vietnam.

children.name: Pontederia korsakowii
children.description: Distribution. China, India, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, Pakistan, Russia, Sri Lanka and Vietnam.

children.name: Pontederia elata
children.description: Distribution. From Myanmar to Malaysia, Thailand and China.

children.name: Pontederia ovalis
children.description: Distribution. Costa Rica, Guatemala, Honduras, Bolivia, Brazil (states of Bahia, Maranhao, Paraiba, Distrito Federal, Goias, Mato Grosso, Espirito Santo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Sao Paulo, Parana, Santa Catarina and Rio Grande do Sul), Colombia, Paraguay and Uruguay.

children.name: Pontederia meyeri
children.description: Distribution. Restricted to Argentina, Paraguay and Brazil (states of Ceara, Mato Grosso and Mato Grosso do Sul).

children.name: Pontederia australasica
children.description: Distribution. Restricted to northern Australia.

children.name: Pontederia brevipetiolata
children.description: Distribution. Gabon, Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, Ivory Coast, Mali, Niger, Senegal and Sierra Leone.

children.name: Pontederia cyanea
children.description: Distribution. Restricted to northern and western Australia.

children.name: Pontederia valida
children.description: Distribution. Southern China and Thailand.

children.name: Pontederia africana
children.description: Distribution. Angola, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, South Africa and Sudan.

children.name: Heteranthera
children.description: Heteranthera — a genus of liliopsidas.

children.name: Heteranthera mexicana S.Watson
children.description: The native range of this species is Texas to NE. Mexico. It is a annual and grows primarily in the subtropical biome.

children.name: Heteranthera missouriensis C.N.Horn
children.description: Phenology. — Flowering July to November. Inflorescences developing in one or two days. Individual flowers opening about two hours after dawn and wilting in early afternoon.

children.name: Heteranthera pauciflora C.N.Horn
children.description: Phenology. — Flowering July to November. Inflorescences developing in one day. Individual flowers open about three hours after dawn and wilt in early afternoon. Most commonly flowers do not elongate out of the spathe and are thus self-pollinated.

children.name: Heteranthera seubertiana Solms
children.description: The native range of this species is S. Mexico, Venezuela to Brazil. It is a annual and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Heteranthera spicata C.Presl
children.description: The native range of this species is Cuba to Hispaniola, Mexico (Jalisco) to Peru. It is a hydroannual and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Heteranthera yucatana Carnevali, J.L.Tapia & J.R.Grande
children.description: Herbs 4.5 – 11.5 cm tall (including the inflorescence), annual, hydrophytic in fresh or brackish water, partially submerged, emergent or paludal, growing at the margins of seasonal ponds or water-filled rock crevices. Roots delicate, diffuse, white and dark blue in dry specimens, not exceeding 8.0 cm long. children.name: Heteranthera lutea
children.description: The native range of this species is Cameroon to Chad, Madagascar. It is a annual or helophyte and grows primarily in the seasonally dry tropical biome.

children.name: Heteranthera gardneri
children.description: The native range of this species is NE. Brazil (to Minas Gerais). It is a hydrosubshrub and grows primarily in the seasonally dry tropical biome.

children.name: Heteranthera limosa
children.description: Heteranthera limosa is an annual flowering plant in the water hyacinth family known by the common names ducksalad and blue mudplantain.

children.name: Heteranthera dubia
children.description: Heteranthera dubia, commonly called water stargrass or grassleaf mudplantain, is a species of aquatic plant in the pickerel-weed family (Pontederiaceae).

children.name: Heteranthera multiflora
children.description: The native range of this species is C. & E. U.S.A., Venezuela to N. Argentina. It is a annual and grows primarily in the subtropical biome.

children.name: Heteranthera oblongifolia
children.description: The native range of this species is S. Mexico, Cuba to Hispaniola, Colombia to Brazil. It grows primarily in the seasonally dry tropical biome.

children.name: Heteranthera peduncularis
children.description: The native range of this species is Mexico to Honduras. It is a helophyte and grows primarily in the seasonally dry tropical biome.

children.name: Heteranthera rotundifolia
children.description: Arable land and market gardens (I1 level 2)

children.name: Heteranthera longirachilla
children.description: The native range of this species is Brazil (Bahia). It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Heteranthera catharinensis

children.name: Heteranthera callifolia
children.description: The native range of this species is Trop. & S. Africa. It is a hydrosubshrub and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Monochorla
children.description: Monochorla — a genus of liliopsidas.

children.description: Pontederites — a genus of liliopsidas.
